title: General mountain guidelines
summary: Good preparation supports good decisions. Match every objective to your experience, the conditions and the people in your group.

items.title: Fitness and training
items.text: Build endurance and strength gradually with activities suited to your objective. Practice carrying your expected pack and include recovery in your plan.

items.title: Permits and access
items.text: Check current permits, closures, seasonal restrictions and local requirements with the land manager before travel.

items.title: Insurance and emergency cover
items.text: Confirm that your policy covers your activity, altitude, evacuation and destination. Understand exclusions and carry the relevant emergency contact information.

sections.title: Gear checklist
checklist: Navigation: map, compass or GPS and spare power
Headlamp with fresh or spare batteries
Food, water and a way to treat water
Sun protection: glasses, sunscreen and head covering
Helmet, harness, rope and technical equipment when required
Trip plan and emergency contact details

items.title: Pacing and teamwork
items.text: Choose a sustainable pace, communicate honestly and check in on the group. Rest before exhaustion compromises judgment.

items.title: Hydration and food
items.text: Drink regularly and eat before energy drops. Adjust your plan for exertion, temperature and the availability of safe water.

items.title: Weather checks
items.text: Compare observed conditions with the forecast throughout the day. Set clear turnaround times and choose a conservative alternative when conditions deteriorate.

items.title: Turnaround decisions
items.text: A summit is optional; returning safely is essential. Agree on decision points in advance and turn back when time, weather, health or terrain requires it.

items.title: Leave No Trace
items.text: Plan ahead, travel on durable surfaces, dispose of waste properly, leave what you find, minimize fire impacts, respect wildlife and be considerate of other visitors.

items.title: Care for local communities
items.text: Follow local guidance, ask before photographing people and places, and support locally led services and conservation.

items.title: Stop and assess
items.text: Protect the group from immediate hazards, provide first aid within your training and keep the person warm and monitored.

items.title: Call for help
items.text: Use local emergency services or an appropriate satellite communicator when needed. Share your location, injuries, hazards and group size; do not rely on mobile coverage.

items.title: Avoid creating more risk
items.text: Do not split the group without a plan, enter terrain beyond your ability or delay calling for help when a serious emergency is developing.
